rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store; a file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build
rules.evidence: The boundary itself is clean and the check is strict. app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:7-11 matches import OR export, either quote style, across sqflite|drift|hive|hive_flutter|shared_preferences|sqlite3|sqlite3_flutter_libs|idb_shim|idb_sqflite|sembast|isar|objectbox|realm plus dart:indexed_db and dart:html, and a second test (:32-42) keeps drivers under lib/spine/store/ even inside the spine. I ran my own scan of all 106 .dart files under app/lib: the only storage-driver imports anywhere are app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10 (package:sqlite3), app/lib/spine/store/store_web.dart:4 (package:idb_shim) and app/lib/spine/store/store_native.dart:8 (path_provider). grep for localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|openDatabase|CacheStorage across app/lib returns zero, so the four files outside the spine that hold dart:js_interop (app/lib/ambient/ambient_web.dart:9, app/lib/capture/hooks_web.dart:4, app/lib/ready_web.dart:1, app/lib/setup/platform_web.dart:1) and package:web (app/lib/media/local_uri_web.dart:4) do not reach browser storage. The one file write outside the spine, app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:24-27, is a content-addressed temp-dir cache of bytes that came from the spine's own blob store, not a second source of truth. What fails is the word 'build': grep for 'flutter test' across every .sh/.py/.yaml in the repo returns nothing, .git/hooks holds no non-sample hook, and there is no .github. bootstrap.sh, run.sh and capture.sh all build and capture without running a single test, so a driver import outside lib/spine/ would ship unless somebody ran `flutter test` by hand.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, docs and code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list
rules.evidence: Eighteen types, and the list agrees. app/lib/spine/types.dart:115-306 holds 18 EventTypeSpec entries; docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:33-50 holds the same 18 in the same order; app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 parses the doc table with a regex and asserts documented == registered plus length >= 14 plus uniqueness, and it ran and passed in my run. Thread rendering is live and held at both ends: app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:166-180 assembles kThreadRenderers from the messenger's bodies, the feelings' and every module's, and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 fails if a type names a renderer that does not exist or a renderer is named by no type. Search is registry-driven: app/lib/spine/search.dart:29-79 reads spec.search.textFields, .facets and .excluded generically. The notification treatment is the leg that does not reach anything. Every spec carries `notify` (types.dart:57) and app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:41-51,115-135 builds a settings row per type from it — but NotificationPrefs.forType (:76-80) and isQuietAt (:71-74), the two functions that decide whether a type may interrupt right now, are called from nowhere: grep for forType|isQuietAt|Announce\. across app/lib outside that one file returns zero. The only arrival-side announcement in the app is app/lib/scope.dart:128-151, whose loop skips every event whose type is not 'feeling' (:137), so the four Notify.interruptive types the doc promises 'sound + first line' for — message, photo, video, voice_note — announce nothing, on either platform (android/app/src/main/kotlin/io/lovetap/desk/Ambient.kt:122-134 `arrival` is reachable only through the 'pocket' channel call at :52, which only a feeling makes). Also stale: types.dart:1 still says 'the same seventeen types'.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line; the commit that added the fourth touched nothing under the first three
rules.evidence: I measured this rather than read it. I added a sixth module — one new file app/lib/modules/probe/probe_module.dart, one import and one list entry in app/lib/modules/registry.dart, one EventTypeSpec in app/lib/spine/types.dart and one row in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md — and ran the full suite: 130 of 131 passed, and the single failure (every_module_is_on_the_desk_test.dart:198, 'the probe: 0 rows, 0 pt') was because my stub drew nothing at all, not because a shared Dart file had been missed. No other file under app/lib needed touching: every consumer is generic over kModules (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:179,223; app/lib/material/assignment.dart:35; app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:42-93; app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:61; app/lib/capture/hooks.dart:475). I then reverted every edit. On history: the four modules dates/todos/calendar/rituals were all added in one commit (d2be5a3d), so there is no fourth-module commit to isolate; the fifth (shelf) went in at ffc5821d, whose file list is registry.dart, its own directory, spine/types.dart, docs/EVENT_TYPES.md, seed data — and app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart, a shared file in a region, which is the cost that has since been removed. What is left uncounted is outside Dart. app/web/push/sw.js:12-25 is a second per-type word table, live (registered at app/lib/ambient/ambient_web.dart:87), and it has already drifted: it names date_event, todo_event, milestone and ritual_kept — four modules' event types, in a file that is not any of those modules' directory — while passed_on, the fifth module's own Notify.quiet type, has no entry, and ritual_kept, which is Notify.none, has one. app/test/module_costs_test.dart:23-27 cannot see any of it because it enumerates only Directory('lib') files ending in .dart. seed/tools/validate.py:54-55,187-189 is a second per-type required-key table for the same reason.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events and never reach the log
rules.evidence: There is no typing or presence type in the registry (app/lib/spine/types.dart:115-306, 18 ids, none of them), and app/lib/spine/spine.dart:207-210 calls specOf(type) before anything else, which throws ArgumentError for an unknown id — so 'typing' cannot be appended even by mistake. The frames travel on their own path: Ephemeral is a separate class (app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-145), the host hands it to a callback and never to the spine (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:264-268), and app/lib/scope.dart:153-164,174-178 sends and receives it with a six-second self-expiring timer and no append. Two tests hold it, both of which ran: app/test/transport_local_test.dart:287-301 sends a typing frame and a presence frame and then asserts r.host.length == 0 and r.client.length == 0, and app/test/reliability_test.dart:117-130 records host.length + client.length unchanged across a typing frame in evidence/reliability.json. Nothing in the app emits on a timer either: every emit call site (app/lib/scope.dart:171, and 27 callers) is a person's action.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread
rules.evidence: Three independent places say so and one of them is the code path. app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:278-284 handles 'read_marker' by moving _readUpto and returning, before the `if (!spec.rowInThread) return;` guard at :286 and before _add at :287, so no ThreadItem is ever created for one. The registry says it too (app/lib/spine/types.dart:199-208, rowInThread: false, search excluded: true, notify: none) and its renderer is the explicit no-op _neverARow (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:139, mapped as 'ink_dries' at :174). Asserted at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34, app/test/thread_types_test.dart:110-120 and app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart:54-58, which replays the seeded year and asserts no item has type read_marker while readUpto is still set.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file — TS_AUTHKEY, a CA private key, a pairing secret — in history as well as the working tree
rules.evidence: I enumerated every object in the repository with `git cat-file --batch-all-objects --batch-check`, took all 3,907 blobs under 2 MB — the content of every file ever committed — and scanned each for tskey-(auth|api|client)-…, '-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----', BEGIN OPENSSH, an assigned TS_AUTHKEY or pairing_secret, AKIA…, gh[pousr]_…, xox…, AIza… , sk-… and Tailscale privkey:. Zero hits of every pattern. `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only` lists no file ever added with a .pem/.key/.p12/.jks/.keystore/.env/.authkey/.pfx/.crt extension. Every occurrence of TS_AUTHKEY in the tree is an environment-variable name or prose about one (bootstrap.sh:12,217-221; tools/tailscale/up.sh:48-60,107-109, which passes --authkey="$TS_AUTHKEY" from the process environment; README.md:23), and .gitignore:12-16 excludes .env, *.authkey and /toolchain/ts/. Structurally there is nothing to leak: the pairing secret is six words minted with Random.secure at run time (app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:43-46), never persisted; only the HKDF-SHA256 output of those words plus the host id is kept (:70-74, stored at app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:146-147 in the device's own store, cleared at :337-338). Caveat, stated: this scans file content, which is what the rule asks about; I did not read commit messages.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key
rules.evidence: The refusal half I measured directly, by driving a real HostServer through a temporary probe test with hand-signed Authorization headers. GET /v1/events returned 401 with no header, 401 with a key derived from the wrong six words, 401 with the right key under another device id, 401 for a replayed nonce (the first use of the same nonce returned 200, the second 401 — app/lib/transport/protocol/wire.dart:129-143), 401 for a timestamp 20 minutes old (kAuthSkew is 5 minutes, wire.dart:11), 401 for a MAC signed over a different path, and 200 only with a correct signature (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:98-103, 128-140; comparison is constant-time at wire.dart:89-96). Two surfaces are unauthenticated by design: the two pairing calls, which returned 403 with no pairing window open (server_io.dart:150-157), and static PWA delivery — an unauthenticated GET / returned 200 with the page when pwaRoot is set (server_io.dart:86-89, 303-329; pwaRoot is passed in the real host at app/tool/host_daemon.dart:105,109). The binding half is checked rather than trusted — addressToServeOn (app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:57-77) refuses a declared address that is not 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 and refuses to serve at all with no tailnet address, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:33-43 proves 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.0.10 and :: are all rejected as declared addresses — but app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:77 reads `boundTo = isUserspace ? '127.0.0.1' : address;`, so in userspace mode the socket is on loopback and reaches the tailnet through the proxy. That is the mode the one recorded real run used: evidence/coldstart.json says host_listener 127.0.0.1:8443 against host_reachable_at 100.68.254.25. It is never a wildcard and never wider than loopback, and the tailnet check still gates it, but the literal claim holds only on a TUN node.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font was downloaded
rules.evidence: I walked assets/ myself: 701 files besides the manifest, 699 of them keys in assets/MANIFEST.json, and every one of those 699 carries a non-empty `generator` (10 distinct scripts: blender/folds/fold.py 240, blender/objects/objects.py 135, blender/paper/tear_relief.py 114, tools/tears/tear.py 57, blender/paper/stocks.py 54, blender/bits/bits.py 44, tools/sound/synth.py 44, tools/handwriting/build.py 7, tools/ink_plate.py 2, blender/shell/desk.py 2) plus a `settings` block. The two unlisted files, assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json and assets/tears/relief.json, are sidecars a generator writes beside its output and are named on the exempt list at tools/check/manifest.py:22-24; running that checker prints '697 files in assets/, 0 without an entry naming their generator' and it is wired into capture.sh:79-80. Nothing is fetched: grep for urlretrieve|urlopen|requests.get|httpx|curl|wget across tools/ and blender/ finds one hit in the whole repo, bootstrap.sh:88, which downloads the pinned toolchain. The three hands are built from skeletons, not from a base face — tools/handwriting/build.py:1-13 states the pipeline and its only inputs are skeletons.json and hands.json. One honest note: the shipped web bundle also carries Flutter's own MaterialIcons-Regular.otf and cupertino_icons, but both are tree-shaken to empty stubs (7,736 and 1,472 bytes in app/build/web), and app/test/nothing_is_set_in_an_icon_font_test.dart:38-52 forbids Icons|CupertinoIcons|IconData|IconButton|Icon( anywhere in app/lib. The only substantive third-party font in the bundle is Flutter's Roboto web fallback (171,676 bytes).

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to
rules.evidence: They pass: `flutter test` gave 'All tests passed!', 131 tests, no skips, and `flutter analyze` reports 37 issues of which zero are errors and two are unused-import warnings in test files. Most of them are unusually honest — app/test/the_hero_holds_eight_notes_test.dart:29-108 loads the real hands, loads the seeded year off disk, drives the app's own scroll handle and then asserts eight sheets of paper with seven whole on the glass; app/test/every_screen_builds_test.dart:47-58 ends every draw with expect(tester.takeException(), isNull). Four do not earn their names. app/test/zz_probe_rows_test.dart:17 ('how tall is one desk row') contains no expect at all, only debugPrint, and a `continue` when the widget it measures is absent — it cannot fail. app/test/with_the_year_in_it_test.dart:121 ('the pulse and the modules have something to say') only draws PulseRegion and UsRegion, so it asserts they build without throwing, in a file whose two neighbours at :106 and :114 do assert non-emptiness. app/test/floors_test.dart:93, inside 'at least fourteen event types, each with a renderer and a notification treatment', reads expect(Notify.values.contains(spec.notify), isTrue) — a tautology on a non-nullable enum, in a file whose own comment at :86-87 says the previous version 'asserted that a non-nullable List was not null'; and floors_test.dart:77-82 ('at least twelve partner-state signals, all of them projected') counts two const lists and asserts nothing about projection — kDeclaredSignals and kPassiveSignals (app/lib/spine/projections/state.dart:38-40) are read by no file under app/lib at all, only by that test. app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart:59-66 ('every module reads the same log and says something from it') I falsified by measurement: my probe module's glance() ignored its argument and returned a constant string, and that assertion passed. Separately, app/test/the_vocabulary_is_out_test.dart:84 emits a hit-test warning on every run — the offset derived for tiles.first does not hit tiles.first — so the tap that the test's name rests on lands on some other widget.

findings.where: forType at :76-80 and isQuietAt at :71-74, against the only arrival path at app/lib/scope.dart:128-151
findings.what: Every event type declares a notification treatment and a person can set one per type in Settings, but nothing at runtime reads either: grep for forType|isQuietAt|Announce\. across app/lib outside notifications.dart returns zero, and the sole arrival-side announcement (scope.dart:137) skips every event whose type is not 'feeling', so the four Notify.interruptive types — message, photo, video, voice_note — announce nothing and the quiet hours a person sets have no effect.
findings.why: Rule 2 requires each type to have a notification treatment; the registry declares one for all eighteen and one type consumes it, so the settings sheet shows a person a control over behaviour the code does not have.

findings.where: the WORDS table at :12-25, live via app/lib/ambient/ambient_web.dart:87
findings.what: A second per-type table outside the registry, in a file app/test/module_costs_test.dart cannot see because it enumerates only Directory('lib') files ending in .dart — and it has already drifted: it names four modules' event types outside those modules' directories (date_event, todo_event, milestone, ritual_kept), gives a word to ritual_kept which the registry marks Notify.none, and has no word for passed_on, the fifth module's own Notify.quiet type.
findings.why: Rule 3's claim that a module costs a directory and one line is enforced by a test that only reads Dart, so the exact failure mode it was written against — a per-type switch drifting from the registry when a module is added — has reappeared one directory away from where the test looks.

findings.where: the whole build path; grep for 'flutter test' across every .sh/.py/.yaml returns nothing, .git/hooks holds no live hook, there is no .github
findings.what: None of the scripts that build or capture runs the test suite, so persistence_boundary_test, spine_schema_test and module_costs_test — the three checks the docs describe as failing the build — only fail if a person runs `flutter test` by hand.
findings.why: Rule 1 asks whether a storage driver imported outside lib/spine/ would fail the build; today it would fail a command nothing in the repository issues.

findings.where: :17-56, testWidgets('how tall is one desk row')
findings.what: The test body contains no expect of any kind — it pumps each module, prints row heights with debugPrint, and skips to the next module when the widget it wants is missing.
findings.why: Rule 9: a committed test that cannot fail is a green line in the suite that measures nothing.

findings.what: expect(Notify.values.contains(spec.notify), isTrue) is a tautology on a non-nullable enum, and 'at least twelve partner-state signals, all of them projected' asserts a count over kDeclaredSignals and kPassiveSignals — two constants no file under app/lib reads — and nothing at all about projection.
findings.why: Rule 9: two assertions weaker than the names they sit under, in the file the build uses to hold the brief's floors.

findings.where: :59-66, 'every module reads the same log and says something from it'
findings.what: The test asserts only that m.glance(log).trim() is non-empty; I falsified it by adding a module whose glance ignored its argument and returned a constant, which passed.
findings.why: Rule 9: the name promises that each module reads the shared log, and a module that never looks at it satisfies the assertion.

findings.where: :121-126, 'the pulse and the modules have something to say'
findings.what: The body draws PulseRegion and UsRegion and nothing more, so the only assertion reached is the takeException check inside draw(); its two neighbours at :106 and :114 do assert that the region put something on the desk.
findings.why: Rule 9: the file's own header says the point is the gap between 'the screen builds' and 'the screen is worth looking at', and this one only tests the first.

findings.what: In userspace mode the socket binds loopback rather than the tailnet address, and that is the mode of the one recorded real run: evidence/coldstart.json records host_listener 127.0.0.1:8443 with host_reachable_at 100.68.254.25.
findings.why: Rule 7 states the host binds only its tailnet address; the tailnet check still gates whether it serves at all and the bind is never wider than loopback, but the literal property is only observable on a TUN node and was not observed.

findings.what: The registry's opening comment says docs/EVENT_TYPES.md 'lists the same seventeen types' while both hold eighteen.
findings.why: Rule 2 asks the doc and the code to agree; the table does, the sentence above it does not, and it is the sentence a reader meets first.

what_is_working: One log, no second store, checked rather than claimed: my own scan of all 106 .dart files under app/lib found storage drivers in exactly three files, all under lib/spine/store/, and zero uses of localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, openDatabase or CacheStorage anywhere. The guard at app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:7-11 covers import and export, both quote styles, thirteen packages and dart:indexed_db/dart:html, and a second test keeps drivers under store/ even inside the spine.

Eighteen event types with the doc and the registry in step and a test that parses the doc's own table to prove it (app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18); the renderer table is assembled from three owners rather than written out (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:166-180) and both ends are held — every declared renderer must exist, every existing renderer must be declared (app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30).

The one-sentence rule is real: search results, notification bodies and the standing line all come through summaryOf (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:186-227), and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:47-84 constructs an event of every type and fails on an ISO timestamp or an underscore reaching a person.

A sixth shared-life module costs what the code says it costs. I built one and ran the suite: a new directory, one import and one line in registry.dart, one EventTypeSpec and one doc row, and 130 of 131 tests passed — the single failure was that my stub drew zero rows, not that a shared file had been missed. Every consumer is generic over kModules (assignment.dart:35, us_region.dart:42-93, search_page.dart:61, renderers.dart:179,223).

Typing and presence cannot become events even by accident: there is no such type, and Spine.append calls specOf(type) first (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:207-210), which throws on an unknown id. Two tests assert neither log grows when a typing frame crosses.

Read markers move a mark and never a row — the projection returns before building one (app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:278-284), the registry says rowInThread: false, the renderer is an explicit no-op, and a golden replay of the seeded year asserts no read_marker item exists while readUpto is still set.

Nothing secret in the repository's entire object store: 3,907 blobs scanned for eleven credential shapes, zero hits, and no key-material file was ever added on any branch. The pairing secret is six words minted with Random.secure and never written down; only the HKDF output is kept, in the device's own store.

The host's authentication is strict where it matters, measured by driving a real server: 401 for a missing header, a wrong key, a right key under another device id, a replayed nonce, a 20-minute-old timestamp, and a MAC signed over a different path — 200 only for a correct signature.

697 of 697 assets carry a manifest entry naming the script and the settings that made them, ten distinct generators, no network call in any of them, and the three typefaces are built from stroke skeletons rather than derived from a downloaded face.

131 tests pass and the analyzer reports no errors; several of the tests are genuinely hard ones — the hero framing test loads the real hands and the whole seeded year before asserting eight sheets of paper with seven whole on the glass.
verdict: The spine holds. There is one log, one storage boundary, and I could not find a second store anywhere in 106 Dart files; typing and presence are structurally incapable of reaching it; read markers move a mark and never a row, in three places that agree. Eighteen event types keep step with their document because a test parses the document. The extensibility claim is the strongest thing here and it is the one I tested rather than read: I added a sixth module and the suite went green on a directory, one line, a registry entry and a doc row, with nothing else under app/lib touched — that is a real answer to the brief's hardest structural requirement. Nothing secret sits in any of the 3,907 blobs this repository has ever held, every asset names the script that made it, and the host answers 401 to a forged, replayed, stale or misdirected request. What keeps this at the floor rather than above it is that two of the registry's promises stop short of the running app. The notification treatment is declared for all eighteen types and settable per type in Settings, and no code reads it: only a feeling announces anything, so a message, a photograph, a video or a voice note arriving is silent, and the quiet hours a person sets do nothing. And the guard that counts what a module costs reads only Dart, so a second per-type table in app/web/push/sw.js — live in the PWA — has already drifted from the registry in both directions, missing the fifth module's own event type and carrying a word for one the registry says is never announced. Under that sit four tests that do not earn their names, one of which I falsified by measurement, and the fact that no script in this repository ever runs the test suite at all: the checks that are described as failing the build fail only a command nobody issues.
